2.heading: my bread:
refs: for a sweet savour unto me:
Heb. savour of my rest, Num 15:3 , 7 , 24

The stated sacrifices and service of the tabernacle having, probably, been greatly interrupted for several years, and a new generation having arisen, who were children or minors when the law was given respecting these ordinances
and as they were now about to enter into the promised land, where they must be established and constantly observed
God commands Moses to repeat them to the people in the following order:
1. Daily morning and evening sacrifices a lamb each time Num 28:3-4
2. Weekly sabbath offerings two lambs of a year old Num 28:9-10
3. Monthly beginning of each month two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, and a kid for a sin offering Num 28:11-15
(1) Passover to last seven days the offerings, two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of a year old, and a he-goat Num 28:16-25
(2) day of first-fruits the sacrifices the same as on the beginning of the month Num 28:26-31

Offering Schedule
1. Daily morning and evening sacrifices a lamb each time Num 28:3-4

3. Monthly beginning of each month two young bullocks, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, and a kid for a sin offering Num 28:11-15
4. Annually
(1) Passover to last seven days the offerings, two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of a year old, and a he-goat Num 28:16-25

27.heading: two young:
refs: Bishop Patrick observes that no peace offerings are appointed in this chapter, which were chiefly for the benefit of the offerers, and therefore in them they were left more to themselves

but burnt offerings, which were purely for the honour of God, and confessions of his dominion, and which figured evangelical piety and devotion, by which the soul is wholly offered up to God, in the flames of holy love
and sin offerings, which were typical of Christ's sacrifice of himself, by which we and our services are perfected and sanctified.
